facts.fact_text: On 6 December 2004, Hyde Park applied to the Chişinău Municipal Council for authorisation to hold a peaceful meeting in front of the Romanian Embassy on 5 January 2005.
The purpose of the planned meeting on 5 January 2005 was to protest against the policy of Romania in respect of Moldovan students.
The application to the Chişinău Municipal Council was signed by Hyde Park's president.
Hyde Park's application to the Chişinău Municipal Council stated that Hyde Park undertook to respect public order and not to block traffic.

Hyde Park (the first applicant) explained that many persons who had expressed their wish to participate in the demonstration were students in Romania and were at home, in Chişinău, only for the winter break.
On 30 December 2004, the Chişinău Municipal Council rejected Hyde Park's application to hold a protest meeting on 5 January 2005.
On 21 February 2005, the Chişinău Court of Appeal dismissed the applicants' action against the Chişinău Municipal Council's refusal to authorise the demonstration.
On 6 October 2005, the Chişinău Court of Appeal again dismissed the applicants' action concerning the refusal to authorise the demonstration in front of the Romanian Embassy.
On 14 December 2005, the Supreme Court of Justice dismissed the applicants' appeal on points of law against the Chişinău Court of Appeal's judgment of 6 October 2005.

Section 6(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be conducted peacefully, without any sort of weapons, and shall ensure the protection of participants and the environment, without impeding the normal use of public highways, road traffic and the operation of economic undertakings and without degenerating into acts of violence capable of endangering the public order and the physical integrity and life of persons or their property.

Section 7 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that assemblies shall be suspended in the following circumstances: denial and defamation of the State and of the people; incitement to war or aggression and incitement to hatred on ethnic, racial or religious grounds; incitement to discrimination, territorial separatism or public violence; acts that undermine the constitutional order.

Section 11(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that not later than fifteen days prior to the date of the assembly, the organiser shall submit a notification to the Municipal Council, a specimen of which is set out in the annex which forms an integral part of the Act.

Section 12(6) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the local authorities can reject an application to hold an assembly only if after having consulted the police, it has obtained convincing evidence that the provisions of sections 6 and 7 will be breached with serious consequences for society.

Section 14(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that a decision rejecting the application for holding an assembly shall be reasoned and presented in writing and shall contain reasons for refusing to issue the authorisation.
Section 15(1) of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995 provides that the organiser of the assembly can challenge the refusal in the administrative courts.

On 6 December 2004, Hyde Park applied to the Chişinău Municipal Council for authorisation to hold a peaceful meeting in front of the Romanian Embassy on 5 January 2005.
The purpose of the planned meeting on 5 January 2005 was to protest against the policy of Romania in respect of Moldovan students.
Hyde Park's application to the Chişinău Municipal Council stated that Hyde Park undertook to respect public order and not to block traffic.
The Chişinău Municipal Council rejected Hyde Park's application on the ground that the municipal police considered the applicants' protest to be unfounded and unwelcome.

The Chişinău Municipal Council's rejection stated that it was the Government of Romania which financed the studies of Moldovan students in Romania and therefore the Romanian authorities were competent to take a decision in respect of the applicants' application of 6 December 2004.
Hyde Park (the first applicant) asked that the case be examined urgently.

Hyde Park (the first applicant) explained that many persons who had expressed their wish to participate in the demonstration were students in Romania and were at home, in Chişinău, only for the winter break.
On 21 February 2005, the Chişinău Court of Appeal dismissed the applicants' action against the Chişinău Municipal Council's refusal to authorise the demonstration.

The Chişinău Court of Appeal observed that the police, the Prosecutor's Office and the Secret Service had obtained information that the applicants intended to breach the provisions of sections 6 and 7 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995.
The Supreme Court of Justice found on 8 June 2005 that there was no evidence that the applicants intended to breach sections 6 and 7 of the Assemblies Act of 21 June 1995.

The Chişinău Court of Appeal dismissed the action on 6 October 2005 on the basis that the holding of a protest meeting in front of the Romanian Embassy could have prejudiced the image of the Moldovan State and of the Moldovan people.
The Chişinău Court of Appeal found on 6 October 2005 that the decision to hold a protest meeting had not been adopted by the council of Hyde Park, as required by Hyde Park's statutes.
The Chişinău Court of Appeal found on 6 October 2005 that Hyde Park's statutes did not contain, in its list of activities, provisions sanctioning actions such as holding protest meetings.

The Supreme Court of Justice dismissed the applicants' appeal on 14 December 2005 on the ground that the holding of a demonstration in front of the Romanian Embassy could have prejudiced the image of the Moldovan State and of the Moldovan people.
